newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to hike public wages 25 pct on January 1.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to hike public wages 25 pct on January 1.

text.p: The Venezuelan government plans a 25 percent wage hike for public sector workers from January 1, Labor Minister Juan Nepomuceno Garrido said on Saturday.
"As we anticipate inflation (in 1997) to be 25 percent, it corresponds to a 25 percent wage increase," he told Reuters at Miraflores presidential palace. He gave no further details.

The planned hike -- which Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff had hinted at last week -- was anxiously expected by Venezuela's 1.3 million civil servants who ended a 15-day strike on Wednesday over the government's delay in paying overdue salary bonuses.

With inflation running at an annual rate of 109 percent but dropping fast, workers have seen their purchasing power eroded. Wages in Venezuela have dropped 53 percent in real terms between 1988 and 1995, according to Central Bank figures.
Through bonuses and other benefits, the minimum take-home income for civil servants was last increased in February to the equivalent of $85 dollars.
